# Generations Wellness Medical Practice

> Physician-led outpatient medical practice at 1801 H Street, Suite C-1, Modesto, CA 95354 (Stanislaus County, California Central Valley). Services: hyperbaric oxygen therapy (hard-shell monoplace chambers, FDA-cleared indications), wound care, IV therapy, physical therapy, occupational therapy, pediatric speech therapy, pediatric therapy, counseling and non-opioid-first pain management. Medical director: Dr. Rajwinder Singh Bahia, MD. Phone (369) 222-0979 or (209) 809-0022. Serves Modesto, Ceres, Turlock, Riverbank, Oakdale, Salida, Manteca, Ripon and Stockton.

Key facts:
- Outpatient only: patients visit, receive care and go home the same day. Visits by appointment.
- Every patient is assessed by a licensed clinician before a treatment plan; providers share one care plan across services.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is offered only for FDA-cleared indications (e.g. diabetic foot ulcers, radiation injury, sudden hearing loss, chronic refractory osteomyelitis).
- In California, physical therapy can start without a referral (limits apply).
- Pages are medically reviewed by Dr. Rajwinder Singh Bahia, MD.
- About the name: Generations Wellness Medical Practice (also called Generations Wellness or Generations Wellness Modesto) is a single physician-led outpatient practice in Modesto, California. It is not affiliated with similarly named wellness businesses in other states.

## Conditions treated with hyperbaric oxygen

- [Conditions HBOT Is Cleared For (FDA & UHMS List) | Modesto](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/): Every FDA-cleared and UHMS-recognized use of hyperbaric oxygen therapy, which are treated in an outpatient center vs. hospital, and what is not cleared.
- [HBOT for Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Emergency Facts](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/carbon-monoxide-poisoning/): Carbon monoxide poisoning is a 911 emergency treated at hospital hyperbaric chambers. Who gets HBOT, how many sessions, and what the evidence shows.
- [HBOT for Crush Injury & Compartment Syndrome: The Evidence](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/crush-injury/): Crush injury and compartment syndrome are surgical emergencies. Where HBOT fits as a hospital adjunct, what the one RCT found, and the outpatient role.
- [Hyperbaric Chamber for Decompression Sickness (The Bends)](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/decompression-sickness/): Decompression sickness is treated by recompression at a hospital or DAN-referred chamber, not an outpatient clinic. What treatment involves; call 911, DAN.
- [HBOT for Diabetic Foot Ulcers | Modesto Wound + HBOT](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/diabetic-foot-ulcer/): HBOT may support healing in selected Wagner grade 3+ diabetic foot ulcers. When physicians consider it, the evidence, and how a course works in Modesto.
- [HBOT Emergency Indications: Gas Embolism, Anemia, CRAO](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/emergency-indications/): Four hospital-only HBOT indications explained: air or gas embolism, severe blood-loss anemia, central retinal artery occlusion, brain abscess. Call 911.
- [HBOT for Necrotizing Fasciitis & Gas Gangrene](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/necrotizing-soft-tissue-infections/): Necrotizing infections are surgical emergencies; HBOT is a hospital adjunct after surgery and antibiotics. What the evidence shows; the later wound role.
- [Hyperbaric Oxygen for Non-Healing Wounds | Modesto, CA](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/non-healing-wounds/): Why some wounds stall and how hyperbaric oxygen may support healing. Which chronic wounds are cleared indications, the evidence, and a course in Modesto.
- [HBOT for Chronic Refractory Osteomyelitis | Modesto](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/osteomyelitis/): Hyperbaric oxygen for chronic bone infection that returns after antibiotics or surgery. Why oxygen matters, the evidence, sessions and coverage. Modesto.
- [Osteoradionecrosis of the Jaw & Radiation Injury: HBOT Care](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/radiation-injury/): Hyperbaric oxygen for radiation jaw necrosis (ORN), pre-extraction dental care, radiation cystitis and proctitis. Evidence, sessions and Medicare coverage.
- [HBOT for Compromised Skin Grafts & Flaps | Modesto, CA](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/skin-grafts-flaps/): When a skin graft or flap is failing, HBOT is an FDA-cleared adjunct. How it may support graft survival, timing, the evidence, and a course in Modesto.
- [Sudden Hearing Loss: HBOT + Steroids Within 14 Days](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/sudden-hearing-loss/): Sudden hearing loss in one ear is urgent. ENT guidelines allow hyperbaric oxygen with steroids within 2 weeks. Sessions, success rates and Modesto referral.
- [HBOT for Severe Thermal Burns: Where It Fits in Burn Care](https://www.generationswellness.net/conditions/thermal-burns/): Severe burns are treated at burn centers. Thermal burns are a listed HBOT indication with limited evidence; scars are not. What is cleared and covered.

## Guides

- [Learn About Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy | Patient Guides](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/): Plain-language guides to hyperbaric oxygen therapy: how it works, side effects, sessions, what to wear, costs, and honest answers on the research.
- [Ear Pressure & Claustrophobia in a Hyperbaric Chamber](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/ear-pressure-and-claustrophobia-in-hbot/): How to clear your ears as the chamber pressurizes, what to do with a cold, and what happens if you feel anxious or want to stop a hyperbaric session.
- [Does Medi-Cal, Kaiser or Blue Shield Cover HBOT in CA?](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/hbot-coverage-medi-cal-kaiser-blue-shield/): Plan-by-plan: Medi-Cal (TAR required), Kaiser, Blue Shield, Anthem, UHC, TRICARE and the VA. What each covers for HBOT and how approval works.
- [How Many HBOT Sessions Do You Need? By Condition](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/how-many-hbot-sessions-do-you-need/): Most HBOT courses run 20–40 weekday sessions, but it depends on the condition. What the sources say by indication, plus scheduling and Medicare rules.
- [Hyperbaric Glossary: ATA, Monoplace & 40 More HBOT Terms](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/hyperbaric-glossary/): Plain-English definitions of hyperbaric terms: ATA, monoplace, barotrauma, air break, TcPO2, Wagner grade, CPT 99183, sham chamber, UHMS, CHT.
- [Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Pros and Cons | HBOT Guide](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/hyperbaric-oxygen-therapy-pros-and-cons/): A balanced look at HBOT: established benefits for cleared conditions, the real downsides (time, cost, side effects, limits), and myths on both sides.
- [Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Side Effects: What to Expect](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/hyperbaric-oxygen-therapy-side-effects/): Common: ear pressure, temporary nearsightedness, fatigue. Rare: oxygen-toxicity seizure, lung effects. Incidence figures, causes and prevention.
- [Is Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Worth It? An Honest Guide](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/is-hyperbaric-oxygen-therapy-worth-it/): It can be for a cleared condition, confirmed by a physician, at medical pressure. Not for unproven uses or 1.3 ATA chambers. A decision framework.
- [What to Wear in a Hyperbaric Chamber (and What Not to Bring)](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/what-to-wear-and-bring-to-hbot/): Wear 100% cotton, skip lotions and electronics. A clear checklist for hyperbaric sessions: glasses, jewelry, makeup, hearing aids, CGMs, food and coffee.
- [HBOT Comparisons: Chamber Types & How to Choose](https://www.generationswellness.net/compare/): Hard vs. soft chambers, mild vs. medical-grade pressure, home vs. clinic, hospital vs. independent centers: plain-language comparisons from Modesto.
- [Soft Shell vs Hard Shell Hyperbaric Chamber: Key Differences](https://www.generationswellness.net/compare/hard-vs-soft-chamber/): Soft-shell (inflatable) vs hard-shell (rigid) hyperbaric chambers: how each is built, oxygen delivery, FDA clearance, fire safety, cost and who needs which.
- [Home Hyperbaric Chamber vs Clinic HBOT: Soft Pods Compared](https://www.generationswellness.net/compare/home-chamber-vs-clinic/): Home soft-pod hyperbaric chambers vs clinic HBOT: pressure, oxygen, FDA-cleared uses, safety, supervision and total cost, to help you decide which fits.
- [Hospital vs Independent HBOT Center: What's the Difference?](https://www.generationswellness.net/compare/hospital-vs-independent-hbot-center/): Hospital hyperbaric programs vs. independent HBOT centers: which conditions need a hospital, cost and billing, insurance, staffing, accreditation, access.
- [How to Choose an HBOT Clinic: 10 Questions to Ask](https://www.generationswellness.net/compare/how-to-choose-a-hyperbaric-clinic/): Ten questions to ask any hyperbaric oxygen therapy clinic: physician assessment, treatment pressure, chamber standards, indications, staffing and pricing.
- [1.3 ATA vs 2.0 ATA Hyperbaric: What the Pressure Means](https://www.generationswellness.net/compare/mild-vs-medical-grade-hbot/): 1.3 ATA mild chambers vs 2.0–2.5 ATA medical-grade HBOT: oxygen dose, FDA clearance, what the evidence supports and when 1.3 ATA is not enough.
- [How Does Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Work? | HBOT Guide](https://www.generationswellness.net/how-hbot-works/): HBOT raises the oxygen dissolved in your blood by breathing near-100% oxygen at 2 to 3 times normal pressure. The physics, the biology, and what ATA means.
- [Monoplace vs Multiplace Hyperbaric Chamber Compared](https://www.generationswellness.net/compare/monoplace-vs-multiplace-hyperbaric-chamber/): Monoplace vs multiplace hyperbaric chambers: how each is pressurized, oxygen hood vs full chamber, attendants, air breaks, fire safety, cost and who suits each.
- [FDA-Cleared Hyperbaric Chamber: What It Really Means](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/fda-cleared-hyperbaric-chamber/): What an FDA-cleared hyperbaric chamber means: 510(k) clearance vs approval, how to look up a chamber, FDA warning on HBOT claims, and questions to ask a clinic.
- [Types of Hyperbaric Chambers: Monoplace, Multiplace, Soft](https://www.generationswellness.net/learn/types-of-hyperbaric-chambers/): The main types of hyperbaric chambers explained: NFPA 99 Class A, B and C, monoplace, multiplace and soft-shell mild chambers, and how to tell which you are in.

## Not offered

- No inpatient or emergency hyperbaric treatment. Emergencies such as carbon monoxide poisoning, decompression sickness or gas embolism are treated in hospital-based chambers; call 911.
- No injections, nerve blocks, spinal cord stimulators, radiofrequency ablation or other interventional pain procedures. Patients who need procedures are referred to specialists.
- No HBOT for off-label, wellness or anti-aging uses; hyperbaric oxygen therapy is offered only for FDA-cleared indications after a physician assessment. Research pages describe evidence for other uses without offering treatment for them.
- IV therapy is physician-ordered after screening; the practice makes no immunity, detox or fatigue claims for IV drips.
